sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (Aolepān Aorōkin Ṃajeḷ)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate or tax distinction; Majuro is the administrative seat of the Registrar of Corporations)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: common-law corporate and commercial jurisprudence modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law and the Model Business Corporation Act, as enacted in the Business Corporations Act (28 MIRC Ch. 2) and applied by the High Court and Supreme Court; customary law retained only for land and traditional-matters; no civil-law or sharia components applicable to corporate, AML/CFT or tax-exempt operations.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States, as amended (2003) - trade, economic assistance, investment and most-favored-nation elements
Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) with the United States (in force) - on-request exchange of tax information
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA) - regional goods-trade preferences
No comprehensive double taxation agreement or standalone bilateral investment treaty is currently in force with the United States, Australia, New Zealand, or EU member states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2014 (P.L. 2014-19), as amended by the AMLCFT (Amendment) Act 2019 (mandatory UBO register), and the AMLCFT (Amendment) Act 2021, administered by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); Business Corporations Act, 28 MIRC Ch. 2; Registered Agents Act 2013; Banking Act 2000. UBO piercing requires written identification of every natural person who ultimately owns or controls 25% or more of the entity through any chain of intermediate companies; where no natural-person UBO is identifiable, the registered agent must obtain and file a declaration of the senior managing official. Nominee shareholdings must be fully disclosed in writing to the registered agent; bearer share instruments, where encountered, must be immobilized and held in the agent's custody.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each UBO, director, and authorized signatory (including identified PEP family members)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin (passport page certified as a true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the issuing state (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State); consular legalization at the RMI Embassy (Washington, D.C.) or an RMI consulate for documents originating in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and/or Certificate of Incumbency of each corporate UBO and intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or licensed registered agent in the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the registry's competent authority; consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter for each UBO and for the corporate UBO (account conduct and identity confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the certifying bank officer plus Hague Apostille where the bank's state is an Apostille member; consular legalization otherwise

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy plus Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration with supporting exhibits (sale contracts, payroll certificates, audited financial statements, capital-gain or inheritance records)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO declarant; exhibits certified by the issuing institutions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the declaration and exhibits; apostille via the competent authority of the exhibiting institution's state; original audited statements may carry a direct apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the licensed registered agent or formation counsel for name reservation, incorporation filings, and registry correspondence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each incorporator and UBO (executed before a notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus apostille, or execution at the registered agent's office with verified identity in accordance with FIU guidance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened pre-onboarding and continuously thereafter against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and other OFAC-administered sanctions lists, UK HMT, EU consolidated lists, and any RMI domestic designations. PEP status (including family members and close associates) is identified through automated screening and triggers enhanced due diligence requiring source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and six-monthly file review. For this Medium_Risk_Enhanced profile (ISIC 4659 used heavy-machinery wholesale with wire-transfer and SWIFT letter-of-credit payment rails), the registered agent applies transaction pattern monitoring for third-party payee anomalies, invoice-packing-list-value mismatches, and trade-based money-laundering red flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro); public-facing registry and name-availability search portal administered on behalf of the Registrar: https://register-iri.com. Filings are accepted electronically through the Registrar's authorized system or at the Majuro counter, in practice via licensed registered agents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be composed of the 26 Latin-script letters of the English alphabet; diacritical marks and special symbols are restricted, while numerals, commas, periods, hyphens, and ampersands are tolerated where they aid distinguishability. The registry compares names after disregarding spaces, punctuation, and entity-type suffixes in the likelihood-of-confusion test. English is the operative registry language; no Marshallese-language or transliteration element is required by statute.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Banker, Trust, Trust Company, Savings, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Surety, Securities, Broker, Investment Fund (use conditioned on prior licensing by the RMI banking, insurance, or securities regulators)
Government, Republic, Municipal, Public Authority, Commission, Agency, Ministerial (requires ministerial consent as implying state sponsorship)
University, College, Academy, Institute, School (requires evidence of an accredited educational operator)
Red Cross, Red Crescent, Rotary, Lions Club, Chamber of Commerce (protected names requiring the consent of the relevant organization)
Cooperative, Foundation, Non-Profit, Association (only permissible where the constitutional form of the entity corresponds to the term used)
Any token that implies a corporate purpose inconsistent with the stated objects or with the Business Corporations Act conduct rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: the applicant, through its licensed registered agent, files a renewal application before expiry of the 30-day reservation and pays the statutory renewal fee (US$75), which yields successive 30-day exclusive reservation windows. Rejection appeal: upon a notice of rejection (typically for conflict with an existing registered or reserved name, or a prohibited token), the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar within 14 days; the Registrar must respond in writing within 21 days; if the conflict is with an earlier reservation, the earlier holder's written consent or the lapse of the earlier reservation is required; judicial review of an adverse final determination lies to the High Court under the RMI Civil Procedure Rules and 28 MIRC Ch. 2's general remedial provisions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. A non-resident Business Corporation must continuously maintain a registered office in the Marshall Islands and a licensed registered agent; both are satisfied by the agent's Majuro office, and the corporation is not required to hold physical premises, hire local staff, or maintain local equipment in the RMI. Remote management and off-island contract execution are consistent with the entity's non-resident tax-exempt classification, and no economic-substance test applies to an ISIC 4659 used-machinery wholesaler operating on this model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the corporate entity (annualized probability below 5% absent an adverse intelligence or FIU suspicion flag). The licensed registered agent is, however, subject to scheduled and risk-triggered on-site examinations by the Registrar of Corporations and the FIU; any unannounced inspection would be directed at the agent's registered office and AML/CFT records rather than at corporate premises, which the non-resident entity does not maintain.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government name-reservation fee (primary and fallback name, 2 x US$75 statutory tariff)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - Registrar's Schedule of Fees under the Financial Management framework

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of incorporation filing fee (Business Corporation, authorized capital up to US$50,000 / 50,000 shares)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - Registrar's Schedule of Fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year annual government maintenance fee (prepaid under the agent's standard incorporation package)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - prevailing annual franchise fee for a non-resident Business Corporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered agent and registered office fee (statutory address, correspondence handling, regulatory filings)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (range US$450 - US$700 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/SDD/AML onboarding package: PEP, OFAC, UN, UK-HMT and EU sanctions screening; risk-tier classification; compliance file assembly
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Medium_Risk_Enhanced profiles

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, Title 22 of the Marshall Islands Revised Statutes: Sections 22-101 to 22-111 (incorporation), 22-201 to 22-207 (Articles of Incorporation), and 22-401 to 22-404 (registered office and registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for such consideration as the Board determines; no escrow account or capital verification filing is mandated for the non-resident Business Corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription of the incorporator for 1,000 common shares, par value US$1.00 each, and authorizes issuance upon full payment of the agreed consideration; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation in the Republic of the Marshall Islands shall be maintained at the address of the duly appointed registered agent, which address is fixed as the Corporation's statutory office for service of process; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed as initial officers, with full authority to execute banking, licensing, and commercial contracts; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts and take all lawful actions necessary to complete the Corporation's formation and ongoing compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General (online e-Registry portal or Majuro counter service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search against the corporate names index; file a Name Reservation application designating a corporate suffix (Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, or approved abbreviation); secure written consent of any proposed registered agent before listing them; the reservation is valid for a renewable statutory period.
required_dossiers: Signed consent of proposed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar or prohibited, file an amended Name Reservation containing up to three alternative names within 10 business days; an administrative refusal may be appealed by written petition to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public or Commissioner of Oaths (Marshall Islands or foreign notary) and the incorporator's counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation including the corporate name, authorized share structure (1,000 common shares at US$1.00 par value), a general purpose clause covering the wholesale remarketing of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers (ISIC 4659), the registered office address, the name and address of the registered agent, and incorporator details; execute and notarize the Articles and the incorporator's written consent.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in triplicate
Certified passport copy of each signing incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any notarial defect or incomplete purpose clause is cured by re-execution; if the Registrar queries a deficiency, file corrective Articles by way of amendment within 14 days of the deficiency notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to the Registrar and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General (filing counter or online e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original and two conformed copies of the notarized Articles; pay the non-refundable US$250 state filing fee plus any courier or expedite surcharge where fast-track service is requested; obtain a stamped receipt and lodgement reference number; retain the certified conformed copy for the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Two conformed copies of the Articles
Duly executed filing fee voucher or wire transfer reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or returned marked DID NOT FILE, cure the stated defect and resubmit within 10 days; ensure the correct fee is re-tendered to avoid a second deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organizational Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Business Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation; convene the organizational meeting or adopt a unanimous written consent of the incorporator and directors to approve the Bylaws, appoint initial directors, elect officers, authorize issuance of share certificates, and ratify pre-formation expenses; record the First Board Resolution in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Written consent in lieu of organizational meeting
Minutes of the First Board of Directors' meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical errors in the corporate name or share capital, request re-issuance by written application to the Registrar accompanied by the original Certificate and supporting evidence; typographical corrections are typically completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Confirmation, Corporate Records, and Banking Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent and the appointed Corporate Services Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered agent services agreement; confirm the registered office address on public record; establish the corporate minute book, share ledger, and statutory records; prepare the Certificate of Good Standing application for banking counterparties; complete the bank's AML/KYC corporate disclosure appropriate to the medium-risk used heavy machinery trading profile.
required_dossiers: Receipt for annual registered agent fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or withdraws consent, appoint a successor agent by board resolution and file the change with the Registrar within 30 days; an unrectified agent vacancy may be cured administratively by the Registrar's designation of a replacement agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Trade and Investment Division, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, in conjunction with the Business License Office of the Office of the Attorney General; no sectoral industrial licensing board mandates an operating permit for wholesale trading of used construction machinery
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Optional Local Business License (Business License Act 1988) and General Trading Registration; not statutorily mandated for the non-resident Business Corporation engaged in offshore wholesale remarketing of secondhand excavators

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Activity Registration tier only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required for indoor warehousing and trading of secondhand excavators absent land disturbance or manufacturing operations; registration is triggered where imported machinery contains residual hydraulic fluids, fuel, oils, or refrigerants requiring controlled handling and disposal
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Marshall Islands EPA Solid Waste Management Regulations and the Marine and Port Waste Regulations; used machinery must be drained of fuel, hydraulic oil, and coolants prior to import or export; uncontrolled VOC or CFC release from compressors is prohibited; any spill or residual fluid must be contained and removed by a licensed waste carrier; storage yards must maintain secondary containment and impermeable paving.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Structural Load Certification from the Majuro Fire Department and the Ministry of Public Works for any storage yard, warehouse, or office premises; Occupational Health and Safety clearance covering forklift and heavy equipment handling, fire extinguishers, emergency egress, and load-rated racking; Port Authority yard pass and Customs bonded-zone approval required where machinery is staged for export.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance and Banking, Republic of the Marshall Islands, administered jointly with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations (RMI Registrar); corporate registration and maintenance filings are submitted through licensed registered agents under the Business Corporations Act (BCA) rather than a public e-filing portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign business corporation (non-resident) obtains its statutory entity registration number by filing Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act through a licensed RMI registered agent. Because the RMI imposes no income tax, capital gains tax, VAT, or sales tax on non-resident entities, no separate TIN or VAT ID is issued. The BCA registration number is used for banking, customs formalities, and corporate records; a customs/port user account may be obtained separately for physical export shipments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election, hybrid-mismatch election, or entity-classification election exists under RMI domestic law. Classification is purely statutory under the BCA: the entity has separate legal personality and is 0% income-taxed in the RMI. If the shareholder is a US person, the US check-the-box election under IRS Form 8832 or US hybrid-mismatch rules may apply for US federal tax purposes, but such an election has no RMI tax consequence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None - No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax in Force; Imports Only Subject to RMI Customs and Excise Tariff
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no indirect-tax turnover registration threshold exists; the RMI levies no VAT/GST/sales tax, and therefore the economic activity threshold is USD 0.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None - no real-time fiscal clearance, API-based reporting, or digital stamping regime exists; standard commercial invoices and statutory books satisfy evidentiary requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable - the RMI imposes no VAT/GST/sales tax. Exported used construction excavators (ISIC 4659) depart the RMI tax-neutral; there is no 0% VAT claim, no output VAT on exports, and no input VAT refund mechanism to substantiate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward entry filed with RMI Customs)
Original Ocean Bill of Lading evidencing physical departure from RMI port
Commercial Invoice (including equipment serial number, year, and weight)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin (issued for consignee-country customs clearance only)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No false zero-rated VAT refund is available to claim because no VAT system operates. Nevertheless, false export declarations, forged customs documents, or misdescribed outward shipments are penalized under the RMI Customs and Excise Act, including fines and/or imprisonment, seizure and forfeiture of goods, retrospective revocation of any customs exemption previously granted, suspension of the exporter's customs user code, and loss of RMI port clearance privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands ('RMI') has no domestic central bank or monetary authority. Pursuant to Section 105 of the Amended Compact of Free Association, the US Dollar is the sole legal tender and monetary policy is effectively delegated to the US Federal Reserve. Prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions is administered by the Banking Commissioner of the RMI Ministry of Finance under the Banking Act 1991 (MI-RC Title 24); AML/CTF supervision is exercised by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Act 2014. OFAC sanctions obligations apply de facto through US correspondent clearing channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility with zero exchange controls. RMI statutes impose no restrictions on current-account or capital-account flows, no central-bank pre-approvals for dividend remittances, loan servicing or liquidation proceeds, and no limitations on foreign-currency account holdings, although the formal banking sector clears exclusively in USD. Profit and capital repatriation by a non-resident Business Corporation is executed via a standard SWIFT MT103 to the shareholder's offshore or US account. The only practical friction arises from FATF-aligned and OFAC-driven enhanced due diligence at the vesting bank and its US correspondent, not from RMI law. RMI's historic presence on the FATF increased-monitoring (grey) list compels robust documentation of source of funds and trade purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. RMI imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Because all export receipts for used construction excavators and rollers are collected in USD, no conversion obligation arises. The exporting BC must nevertheless retain a complete audit trail of the full commercial value in each transaction — bills of sale, bills of lading, customs declarations and bank credits — to satisfy the receiving bank's trade-based money laundering controls and to demonstrate that no over- or under-invoicing has occurred.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD Demand Account
Operational USD Demand Account / Interest-Bearing Money Market Account
Operational USD Account / Trade Finance and LC Issuance Window

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. RMI law does not license e-money institutions or payment service providers; only banks licensed under the Banking Act 1991 may lawfully hold deposits or operate payment accounts in RMI. Foreign digital EMIs (FCA- or EU-licensed) lack any RMI presence and, due to the RMI's offshore-registry risk profile and FATF increased-monitoring status, most regulated EMIs will refuse onboarding of a non-resident BC trading used heavy machinery. At most, a foreign EMI may be used as a low-value collection point (single transactions under USD 25,000) with automatic sweeps to the primary BOMI account; all trade settlements and LC operations must execute on licensed bank rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid with strong in-person presumption. For a non-resident BC classified as 'Medium-Risk Enhanced', domestic banks require a certified excerpt from the RMI Registrar, a duly notarised board resolution with apostilled director identification, and either a physical interview at the Majuro branch of the relevant bank or a live video interview witnessed by the RMI registered agent. In practice, at least one director, or a formally appointed attorney-in-fact under a notarised power of attorney, must be able to attend a physical or consular-attested interview. Purely documentary remote opening without any interview is not available to non-resident taxpayers of this profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: RMI offshore-registry and historic FATF grey-list perception; any non-resident entity is automatically placed in Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing; certified Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws; Registered Agent Certificate with local address; complete UBO declaration covering all natural persons holding >10%; passport-grade ID and proof of residential address of each director; three-year bank reference from an OECD-listed bank; sworn source-of-wealth affidavit; RMI tax-exempt status confirmation; and a written confirmation that no bearer shares are outstanding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of any physical trading premises or employees in RMI creates shell-company risk indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed registered-office and corporate-services agreement; letter from the resident agent confirming physical accessibility and record retention; opening balance sheet with 12-month cash-flow forecast; equipment depot and logistics contracts in supplier and buyer jurisdictions; and the BC's commercial website or dealer registrations evidencing an active used-machinery remarketing operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Used hydraulic excavators and rollers (ISIC 4659, HS 8429.52) carry dual-use and export-control diversion risk to embargoed or military-adjacent end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-specific compliance file including end-user and end-use certificates for each buyer; OEM serial-number registry and model list; independent certified equipment appraisal; full chain of title from supplier invoice to bill of lading to customs entry; and a sanctions-screening log (OFAC, EU, UN) run on every counterparty before each wire or LC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire and LC flows from or to high-risk trade corridors (e.g., CIS, transit hubs, Middle East, West Africa) trigger Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical and projected payment matrix with vessel and container details; financial standing and regulatory status report for each trading counterparty; the BC's written AML/CTF manual with designated Compliance Officer and training records; and letters of indemnity or source-of-funds declarations for each individual wire above USD 100,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque pricing of second-hand equipment compared to new units invites valuation and TBML scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each machine, an independent survey report from a certified inspector or OEM-affiliated valuer documenting fair market value; a documented price-reasonableness analysis against industry auction indices; and the full procurement cost stack — inspection, transport, insurance and repair invoices — demonstrating arm's-length commercial margins.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are executed by SWIFT MT103 in USD from the shareholder's own account to the BC's BOMI operating account. Field 70 must state the purpose as 'INCREASE PAID-IN CAPITAL' and reference the corporate resolution number. Pre-filed with the receiving bank: signed capital contribution resolution, subscription agreement, extracted shareholders' register, and a source-of-funds attestation letter from the remitting bank. No RMI central-bank or ministry approval is required for capital import; however, for amounts above USD 1,000,000, the bank may escalate a 'receipt of funds' inquiry to the FIU and will require a director-certified resolution and a bank reference letter. For time-sensitive closings, use same-day Fedwire settlement through the US correspondent; otherwise the standard SWIFT MT103 with two-day value suffices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for used excavators settle via SWIFT MT103 with field 70 carrying the invoice number, bill-of-lading reference, and equipment serial numbers. For recurring or high-value purchase programs (above USD 250,000 per transaction), use an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and confirmed by a first-class US or Asian bank, with 90% payable against shipping documents and 10% against final inspection certificate. A standby LC (SWIFT MT760) may be added as a performance bond to secure volume allocations. All USD clearing runs through the US correspondent network via CHIPS or Fedwire; same-day settlement is available for instructions received before 11:00 AM Majuro time (UTC+12). Maintaining a minimum operating liquidity buffer of USD 150,000 is recommended to support the bank's LC facility and overdraft commitments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward contracts (USD/EUR, USD/JPY) executed through an OECD-headquartered international bank; no RMI Ministry of Finance consent is required.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) used exclusively to hedge non-USD supplier invoices denominated in EUR or JPY, documented against firm rolling purchase orders.
Cross-currency swaps (USD into EUR/JPY) for import capex refinancing, permissible only with licensed international banks and tied to a specific equipment acquisition.
Vanilla currency options and zero-cost collars for hedging used-machine purchase price exposure in EEA or Japanese supplier currencies.

Since the BC is USD-functional and all trade settlements occur in USD, FX hedging is optional; any instrument must be clearly linked to an underlying invoice to satisfy trade-based AML documentation requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Statement of Share Capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before the last day of the month of each annual incorporation anniversary; initial report due within 60 days after incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of US$100 plus 10% monthly interest; continued non-filing for 90 days triggers administrative strike-off and loss of legal standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (collected on behalf of RMI National Treasury)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable concurrently with the annual report; no separate return for non-resident tax-exempt corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues at 10% per annum; unpaid tax prevents issuance of Certificate of Good Standing and may result in administrative strike-off after 3 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent at the registered office in Majuro (private contractual filing copy retained for verification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal confirmed on the anniversary date of the registered agent agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent results in involuntary dissolution by the Registrar after 60 days' notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Share Transfer Annual Confirmation to Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (maintains non-public UBO and share transfer records for regulatory inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed with the annual report; within 15 days after any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Material omission may subject the corporation to a fine of up to USD 5,000 and the responsible officer to disqualification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-resident Business Corporation not conducting business, holding property, or having employees in the Marshall Islands. An independent audit becomes mandatory only if the corporation holds a bank, insurance, or similar licensed activity, obtains a Foreign Investment Business License, or if shareholders holding at least 10% of outstanding shares petition for an audit under the Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCCA) requires accounting records sufficient to reflect financial position; financial statements may be prepared under IFRS or US GAAP, both being acceptable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain a certified beneficial ownership schedule at least annually and before each share transfer. The annual report to the Registrar must summarize issued shares and transfers during the reporting period. Each transfer requires a directors' resolution, share certificate cancellation/reissue, and Register of Members update. No public UBO registry filing is made; records remain with the registered agent subject to inspection by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit and Registrar of Corporations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger with transfer details)
Minute Book with shareholder and director resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required; if voluntarily ordered, USD 3,500 - 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporations with a valid Tax Exemption Certificate; the general RMI corporate income tax rate is 11.5% and applies exclusively to RMI-source business income of non-exempt entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 251(d) of the RMI Income Tax Act grants an absolute exemption from RMI income tax to qualifying non-resident domestic corporations deriving income solely from sources outside the Marshall Islands. Foreign-source income is not subject to RMI taxation. No capital gains tax, no payroll tax, no social security levy on foreign employees, no VAT/GST, and no annual franchise tax on gross income. The only recurring state-imposed charge is the Business Corporation annual registration fee payable to the Registrar of Corporations, which ranges from USD 200 for authorized capital up to USD 5,000,000 and increases proportionally above that threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Revenue and Taxation Department — Form IT-2 (Non-Resident Corporation Annual Nil Return) filed electronically via the RMI Tax E-Filing Portal (portal.rmi-tax.com); Tax Exemption Certificate renewal via Form IT-110. Registration compliance with the Registrar of Corporations is effected through the Annual Corporate Report Filing (BCA Form AR-1) submitted through the RMI Online Corporate Registry.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual income tax nil return is due on the last day of the third calendar month following the close of the fiscal year (calendar-year companies: 31 March). The BCA Annual Corporate Report and registration fee are due on the anniversary date of incorporation; a grace period of 60 days applies before penalty accrual.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registration number, date of incorporation, fiscal year-end date, and Tax Exemption Certificate reference number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as registered with the RMI Registrar; insert the certificate number issued under Section 251(d). No RMI taxpayer identification number is required for a nil return; enter the corporate registration number as the alternate identifier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income derived from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including local trading, services rendered in Majuro or Ebeye, and RMI real property income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident exempt corporations must declare zero RMI-source receipts. If any RMI-source receipt exists, the Tax Exemption Certificate is nullified and a full taxable return must be filed immediately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statistical declaration of worldwide gross receipts derived outside the RMI, including proceeds from resale of used construction excavators, spare parts, and logistics commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the aggregate foreign-source turnover on a best-efforts basis. This field does not create RMI tax liability; it is used for OECD BEPS statistical monitoring by the RMI Revenue and Taxation Office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Non-Resident Status and Permanent Establishment Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Formal attestation that the corporation has no physical office, branch, permanent establishment, employees, or independent agent habitually concluding contracts in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Requires a statutory declaration signed by a director or corporate officer. Failure to update this declaration during the tax year is treated as a fraudulent claim and triggers retrospective revocation of exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of cross-border sales and purchases with related parties, including intercompany commission arrangements with the trading principal and any margin retained by the RMI entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Although RMI imposes no tax on foreign-source income, complete the schedule to evidence that the RMI entity retains only a routine servicing margin (typically less than 20 basis points per transaction). Leave blank only if no related-party dealings occurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Manual or digital signature of a duly authorized director, with date and capacity; affirmation under penalty of perjury that the information is true and complete.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director may sign electronically. The director personally warrants the accuracy of the non-resident and RMI-source representations; false certification exposes the signatory to criminal penalty under the RMI Criminal Code.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual report incurs a flat penalty of USD 250 plus an additional monthly surcharge of USD 50 (capped at USD 1,000), and the company loses good standing and may be administratively dissolved after 90 days in default. Late filing of the income tax nil return triggers a 5% per month late-filing penalty on any assessed tax (not applicable to nil returns) and a minimum administrative penalty of USD 500 for non-filing; continued non-filing results in automatic revocation of the Section 251(d) exemption and loss of corporate good standing with consequential banking due-diligence rejection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not impose any withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Business Corporation to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident, nor any secondary corporate tax on distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive double tax treaty network; only sectoral agreements limited to international ship and aircraft transportation exist (e.g., with the United States). Consequently, no treaty relief application is required or available for dividend flows. The zero-rate outcome is achieved through domestic statutory exemption: the paying RMI BC simply withholds nothing and does not report the distribution. If an inbound investor jurisdiction requires a Residence Certificate to demonstrate RMI tax residence for its own foreign-tax-credit purposes, the corporate officer submits a written request to the RMI Revenue and Taxation Office; the Department issues a Certificate of Residence on letterhead confirming the entity's non-resident exempt classification; the request must be accompanied by a certified copy of the Tax Exemption Certificate and a declaration of the shareholder registry. No Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) is issued for non-resident entities under RMI law; the Department instead issues a Certificate of No Tax Liability, which serves the equivalent evidential function before foreign tax authorities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 0% on royalties from trademarks, dealership rights, or industrial know-how paid by an RMI BC to non-residents; 0% on interest on intercompany shareholder loans or bank debt paid to non-residents. Treaty rates: no RMI comprehensive DTA coverage exists; therefore the domestic 0% rate is final and no foreign withholding tax credit recovery mechanism is available within RMI.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File or Master File thresholds have been enacted in the Marshall Islands. The RMI Income Tax Act applies the arm's length principle for related-party dealings, but this is inoperative where the non-resident BC is tax-exempt and derives no RMI-source income. A best-practice threshold of USD 2,000,000 aggregate intercompany turnover is applied by international banks and foreign tax authorities; for the used excavator remarketing business, the RMI entity typically acts as a limited-risk distributor and should retain contemporaneous documentation — including intercompany agreements, pricing matrix, and a TNMM benchmarking study demonstrating a routine return below 0.2% of gross resale value — in order to satisfy the source-country audit requirements of the markets where the heavy machinery is physically deployed.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance Regulations Act 2021 applies exclusively to companies that are RMI tax residents — i.e., entities incorporated in RMI, except those that have established tax residency in a foreign jurisdiction and submit an annual declaration to that effect. A Non-Resident Business Corporation engaged in offshore remarketing of used construction excavators is outside the ESR scope because (a) it is not an RMI tax resident for income tax purposes, and (b) it does not conduct any relevant activity within the territory of RMI. The applicable classified activity would be 'distribution and service center' if conducted in the RMI, but physical operation is entirely offshore. Economic substance obligations therefore rest with the principal trading entity in the foreign jurisdiction where management, employees, and physical storage for the excavators are located. The RMI BC must nonetheless file a signed Annual ESR Non-Resident Declaration with the Registrar to maintain its exempt status; failure to file this declaration triggers automatic ESR review, statutory penalties up to USD 20,000, and possible director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through False Exemption Certification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing an annual return declaring zero RMI-source receipts while the entity is in fact earning RMI-source income through a sales office, warehouse, or dependent agent on Majuro Atoll, or deriving income from equipment physically operated by RMI personnel; also covers backdating the Section 251(d) certification or concealing a permanent establishment in RMI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the Tax Exemption Certificate retroactively to the start of the fiscal year; full reassessment of all RMI-source income at the progressive corporate rate culminating in 11.5%; a 25% negligence penalty and a 50% fraud penalty on the underpayment; monthly interest accrual at 1.5% on outstanding principal; immediate deregistration of the Business Corporation and publication of the dissolution in the RMI gazette; the Revenue and Taxation Department may preserve an in-rem lien over all corporate assets held in the RMI, including receivables due from local dealers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director who signs a false nil return or exemption declaration is jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax, penalties, and interest without the benefit of the corporate shield; the director additionally faces criminal prosecution under Section 12 of the RMI Income Tax Act and the Criminal Code with fines up to USD 25,000, imprisonment for up to five years, a travel ban preventing departure from the RMI pending full settlement, and a lifetime prohibition on serving as an officer or director of any RMI-registered entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial Ownership Concealment and Shell Company Abuse (AML)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the RMI Business Corporation as a shell with nominee shareholders or nominee directors who disavow any knowledge of the beneficial owner; failure to disclose and continuously update the beneficial ownership schedule in the confidential RMI Central Register; processing of excavator sale proceeds through the RMI entity where the ultimate customer, end-user, or consignor is a sanctioned entity or a politically exposed person subject to international sanctions, particularly in jurisdictions under OFAC or EU restrictive measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) administrative penalties of up to USD 200,000 per incidence; mandatory suspicious activity reporting failures exposed; freezing orders over bank accounts and tradeable assets under the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2016 (as amended); deregistration of the corporation; referral to the US Department of Justice or foreign authorities through the Mutual Legal Assistance framework; reinstatement of FATF greylist countermeasures may subject the entity to enhanced foreign scrutiny and asset blocking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and beneficial owners failing to disclose UBO information are personally liable for fines up to USD 100,000 and imprisonment up to ten years; the FIU may apply to the High Court for a travel ban and passport surrender; proceeds generated through the concealed shell arrangement become recoverable via criminal asset forfeiture, and directors who knowingly facilitated sanctions evasion face extradition risk and personal foreign civil judgments for conversion and fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Persistent Default on Annual Registration Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the BCA Annual Corporate Report and pay the annual registration fee for more than 90 days past the statutory deadline; continued operation and invoicing while the Registrar has formally declared the entity not in good standing; failure to notify the Registrar of a change of registered agent or a change of non-resident status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of USD 250 plus a monthly surcharge of USD 50; automatic administrative dissolution after 90 days of default; dissolution extinguishes the legal personality of the corporation, voiding the validity of all contracts, wire transfers, bills of lading, and letters of credit executed after the dissolution date; contracts entered in the name of a dissolved corporation are unenforceable, and all proceeds remitted after dissolution are considered funds received without legal capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who continue to trade during a period of involuntary dissolution are personally liable in contract and tort for all obligations incurred during the void period; the veil is pierced as a matter of the RMI Business Corporations Act; directors may be required to make restitution to counterparties, face a High Court injunction preventing their departure from RMI, and be stripped of their directorships in any domestic or international entity registered in the RMI for a period of five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Base Erosion and Artificial Substance Abuse (BEPS Countermeasures)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the used construction excavator trading transaction chain so that the RMI Business Corporation interposes itself between a manufacturing or source-country seller and an end-market buyer exclusively to defer or eliminate source-country corporate tax, while the RMI entity maintains no physical presence, no employees, no bank account in RMI, no board meeting documentation, and no commercial rationale beyond holding title during shipment; this arrangement is often flagged by foreign tax authorities as a treaty-shopping conduit operating in a blacklisted zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI itself imposes no new tax, but the foreign revenue authorities will apply their CFC rules, controlled-foreign-corporation regimes, and transfer-pricing recharacterization to repudiate the interposition; underpayment assessments at 10% to 30% in the source market, plus interest and penalties; the RMI entity may be placed on the public EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions if structural abuse becomes systemic, triggering defensive withholding regimes in every EU member state; adverse FATF ratings may follow, leading to enhanced due-diligence rejection by all correspondent banks and a functional inability to open or maintain the corporate bank accounts required for cross-border wire transfers and SWIFT letters of credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who architect or consent to the interposition without valid economic substance face civil restitution claims in the foreign revenue jurisdiction, personal assessment orders under the foreign CFC legislation, and fraudulent conveyance actions brought by creditors; foreign courts may issue travel bans pursuant to international tax-judgment recognition protocols, and extradition proceedings are available under the RMI extradition legislation for indictable tax offences; professional license revocation applies to attorneys or corporate service providers who knowingly facilitate the artificial arrangement.
